subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw accept a reserved no-op `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` config contract now, or wait until the saturated-session guard runtime/default policy is approved?
rationale: The PR adds a public config/default surface that current main does not use, while the canonical compaction guard and rate-limit issues still require maintainer product decisions.

options.title: Defer Until Runtime Contract Is Approved
options.body: Keep the PR open as candidate source work, but require maintainers to approve the namespace, defaults, and runtime behavior before merging any config surface.

options.title: Accept Reserved Config Now
options.body: Maintain the no-op reserved contract intentionally, accepting that future guard behavior must remain compatible with this shape.

options.title: Replace With Runtime-Backed PR
options.body: Close or supersede this config-only branch after opening a narrower PR that includes the approved runtime behavior and proof.

recommendation.title: Defer Until Runtime Contract Is Approved
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open as candidate source work, but require maintainers to approve the namespace, defaults, and runtime behavior before merging any config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blocker is the compaction guard product/default contract, and steipete has the clearest adjacent safeguard ownership signal from history and prior triage.
